reason: The Commission confirms the programme was adopted on 28 May 2025, and its 2026 report finds tangible progress on the programme's key performance indicators and continued implementation. Government material records a funding gap of about MDL 225 million and capacity limits in the lead bodies, so delivery of the action plan is not yet complete.

The text is a draft law still under inter-institutional consultation, with comments being accepted and the quota provisions removed. It provides that it would enter into force on 1 June 2027 and repeal Law No. 200/2010, and no source reports its adoption.
The amendment to Law No. 105/2018 is a draft in consultation, with ministries still proposing changes to its definitions and entry-into-force clause. No source reports its adoption.

The portal has operated since 2011 and holds about 1,268 datasets, and a 2024 international partner report describes it as a one-stop shop for public sector data. The same body of evidence finds that the portal is still lacking in use and needs updating, so use at scale is not shown.

Parliament adopted the law on 10 April 2025 and the Commission confirms it entered into force on 1 January 2026. The regulator was renamed under it, but in 2026 the secondary acts needed to implement it were still being drafted, and a civil society source notes only partial compatibility with Directive (EU) 2018/1972.

The Commission reports that EVOSign was launched, and the e-Governance Agency says it has run in pilot mode in the production environment since 8 August 2024 and is available in the app stores. Other public bodies consulted on the 2025-2027 programme state that it is only at the pilot and testing stage, has not been launched and lacks the confirmations needed for use, so the sources conflict on whether it is in operation; it is also planned to be absorbed into the digital wallet.

The audit found about 198,900 permits issued through SIA GEAP, although only 16 of 31 permit-issuing institutions used it fully or partly. In 2025 the communications regulator moved all its permits onto the system and issued 109 of 303 technical permits through it, which shows actual use, though not by every issuing body.

The Commission reports that an EESSI action plan was approved, and the authorities are preparing the digital infrastructure and the ANOFM and CNAS systems for interoperability. The actual connection still depends on technical documentation from the Commission and a technical solution yet to be chosen, so Moldova is not connected to EESSI.
The orders appear only as drafts in the 2025 accession programme's legislative plan, and no source reports that any of them was issued.
The Commission confirms that Moldova joined the EU Roam Like at Home area on 1 January 2026 after aligning with the EU roaming acquis. No source gives data on use of roaming under the scheme.

The Commission reports that bilateral social security agreements were concluded in 2022 and that Moldova had agreements with 13 EU Member States and Türkiye by 2023, and the Government reported 17 agreements with EU Member States in 2025. The agreements are in force, but no source gives data on claims or benefits handled under them, and agreements with ten Member States remain to be concluded.

The Commission reports that a normative framework implementing the cybersecurity law was approved through several Government Decisions to align with the NIS 2 Directive, that the framework was amended to adjust institutional roles, and that secondary legislation on cyber incidents and 5G security was adopted in 2026. The sources describe the acts approved but not how they are applied.

The Commission reports that Moldova migrated to NCTS Phase 5 nationwide on 1 October 2024, completed the Phase 6 rollout in September 2025 and connected it to the common transit network in November 2025, and lists it among the operational customs systems. Nationwide use for transit declarations shows application at scale.

The Commission and the Government list MPass among the government platforms implemented, and an international partner describes it as the authentication service for public e-services. Government consultation material gives 208,500 identifiers authenticated from 2023 to September 2024, but no independent source reports on use.

An international partner reports that MCabinet was launched in October 2020 and gives access to 17 data blocks. The Government reports that unique authenticated users rose from 92,619 in 2023 to 176,855 in the first three quarters of 2024, but this rests on its own reporting.

Government Decision No. 677 of 8 October 2025 approved the measures to implement the Unitary Design Model for all public service providers. The Government reports the work as in progress and says the model will be applied gradually, starting with MSign and MPass, so application across services is not yet shown.

The strategy was carried out and has expired. The Commission finds its implementation only partially successful, with 6 of 12 targets met and weak results on online public services and their take-up, and the Government's own final report also records failures from underfunding and limited capacity.

An international partner reports that the Government approved the strategy in 2023, and the Commission describes its priorities. These items give no evidence on how far its digitalisation measures have been carried out.

The electronic health record is planned, with its concept and regulation due by the end of 2026 and the system for 40% of the insured population by 2027. In 2026 the Government reports only that the draft Government Decision on it is being prepared.

Government Decision No. 822/2025 approved the concept of the register's information system and the regulation on keeping it. The Cyber Security Agency reports that the terms of reference for building the register are still being drafted, so the register is not yet in operation.

The law has applied since 2016, and the regulator reports about 21 administrative procedures under it, 218 entities that have submitted access conditions and 1,932 registered access contracts at the end of 2025. These figures come from the regulator's own reporting, which also records uneven application and disputes over access fees.

The Government reports that new identity cards with a chip and an integrated qualified signature certificate have been issued since 31 March 2025, and a civil society source reports that one million such cards were issued in 2025. This shows issue at scale, though no source reports how often the signature function is used.

The new SI EMRU is planned under the public administration reform programme to be functional in 2026, and in 2026 the data protection authority was still commenting on its design. The Commission found the previous system not functional, and no source reports the new system in operation.

The Commission reports that the Council renewed Moldova's access to the EU Cybersecurity Reserve for a further year in July 2026. The Cyber Security Agency reports that it activated the mechanism successfully, but this rests on its own account.

An international partner reports that MPower was launched in 2020 and lets people create electronic powers of attorney with the same value as notarised ones, and the Government lists it among its working platforms. No source gives data on its use.
Strengthening the Centre's capacity is set out as a planned measure. At the end of 2025 it had 36 staff against a limit of 45, and no source reports the strengthening carried out.

The State Chancellery approved the methodology on institutionalising life events by Order No. 331 of 18 December 2025. The Government reports the reorganisation as in progress, and no source shows services already reorganised around life events.

The Commission reports that the updated infrastructure access tariffs entered into force on 1 March 2026 and that the reference offer was published on the incumbent operator's website. The regulator also reports issuing Board decisions where access disputes could not be settled by dialogue.

The concept and register regulation were approved by Government Decision No. 323/2021, and the Government lists the Semantic Catalog among its new platforms and reports employment data integrated through it. An international partner finds that the open data portal it supports is still lacking in use.

The programme was approved by Government Decision No. 306/2025, and ministries cite its actions when drafting laws, such as the Chapter 2 action on unemployment benefit coordination and the data governance law. The evidence on its delivery comes only from government sources.

The regulator reports that it has measured mobile service quality since 2019, covered 45 localities and 35 national roads, and added 5G networks to the 2025 measurements. The evidence comes only from the regulator's own report.
The Government adopted Decision No. 562/2025 in September 2025, as a civil society source confirms. Its implementation is still listed as a task, and no source reports how providers are complying.

The Commission reports that SIENA has been rolled out to several law enforcement authorities and that exchanges through it have increased. Government sources date the connections of the Criminal Assets Recovery Agency to February 2020 and of the National Anticorruption Centre to March 2023.

The Commission reports that the electronic prescription system has been operational since 1 April 2024 for reimbursed medicines and medical devices and was modernised by 2026. The Government reports over 270,000 reimbursed prescriptions a month at the end of 2024, but no independent source reports on its use.

The Commission's Reform Agenda document confirms that Moldova has established its Reform Agenda, which sets out the digital, cybersecurity and connectivity reforms with deadlines to 2027. These items give no evidence on how far the reforms have been delivered.

The Commission reports that the first European Digital Innovation Hub in Moldova was launched in April 2026, after the e-Governance Agency prepared the consortium and application in 2025. No source yet reports on the hub's activity.
The Government lists MDocs among the new platforms developed, and an international partner gives it the same operating status as the other government platforms. No source gives data on its use.

The orders appear as drafts in the 2025 accession programme. The Commission reports in 2026 that the technical standards, procedures and formats for EURES were developed, but no source reports that the orders were issued.
The new posts appear only as planned measures in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports that they were created or filled.
The draft decision was suspended by the Public Services Agency in August 2025, then resumed under a new number in 2026 and is awaiting examination by the Government. No source reports its approval.

The "Migration" information system is being developed with IOM support and EU funding, with work planned to end in June 2026. The latest source in 2026 still describes it as under development, and none reports that it was launched.

Operators agreed in May 2023 to lower roaming tariffs between Moldova and the EU from January 2024, and the Government reports the reduced tariffs applied from 1 January 2024. The Government describes this as a temporary mechanism for 2024 and 2025, followed by Moldova joining Roam Like at Home on 1 January 2026.

A civil society report states that the Public Services Agency accepts registration documents signed with a qualified electronic signature and that over 723 organisations have used this since 2022, with 359 online applications in 2025. Registration cannot yet be completed fully online.

The Commission describes Moldova as an active participant in TRACES NT with agreed harmonised certificates. Further access is still planned, and the Government notes that full integration with EU systems such as TRACES remains to be achieved.

Moldova joined the Digital Europe Programme on 19 February 2024 and the Commission reports that Parliament ratified the association agreement in May 2024. The Commission also reports the first European Digital Innovation Hub, prepared under the programme, launched in April 2026.

The Commission reports that Moldova amended its secondary legislation to align with the remaining EU roaming acquis and joined Roam Like at Home on that basis on 1 January 2026, which shows the rules being applied.

The Commission reports that the roadmap and timeline for interoperability of the tax administration with EU information systems for 2026 to 2029 was approved in November 2025. No source yet reports its delivery.

The Commission reports that technical standards, procedures and formats for matching vacancies and CVs with the EURES portal were developed. Interoperability of the ANOFM system with EURES is still described as a measure to be carried out, and no source reports it working.
The Commission reports that the law on access to property for public service providers, aligning with the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, was adopted in June 2026. No source yet reports its application.
The Strategic Delivery Unit is set out as a planned structure in the 2023 strategy and again in the 2024 action plan, and no source reports that it was established.

Romanian courses for EU and EEA citizens and their children are planned under a new edition of the national programme for 2026 to 2028, to be drafted in 2025. No source reports the new programme adopted or courses provided.

Government sources agree that the geo-blocking law was adopted in 2025 and that it only partially transposes Regulation (EU) 2018/302. They conflict on the law's number: the National Accession Programme names it Law No. 54/2025 and gives Law No. 53/2025 to the platform-to-business law, while the 2025 progress report on the digital strategy names it Law No. 53/2025.
The action plan on alignment with the European Health Data Space Regulation is planned, and in 2026 the Government reports only that it is being drafted.

The Government reports that the civil status records system was tested, piloted and handed over to the Public Services Agency in August 2025 and went into production on 3 November 2025. No source reports on its use since launch; in 2023 an international partner found that some offices still recorded requests on paper.

A civil society source reports that Moldova and Romania signed the agreement in February 2022 and, citing the two regulators, that roaming internet traffic rose sharply in 2022 and the average roaming basket cost fell by almost 70% for Moldovan users. The evidence dates from 2022, and no source says how the agreement relates to Moldova joining Roam Like at Home in 2026.
The Commission reported in 2021 and again in 2023 that the draft law had been awaiting its second reading in Parliament since November 2018.

Moldova later adopted Law No. 195/2024 on personal data protection, which is recorded as a separate intervention. No source says whether the 2018 draft became that law or was withdrawn, so its status at the freeze date cannot be established.
The Commission reports that Moldova and Spain signed the social security agreement in July 2022.

The Commission reports that the agreement with Spain entered into force in June 2024, and the Government lists the arrangement, agreement and forms for Spain. No source gives data on cases handled under it.

The Commission reported in 2024 that the draft Customs Service IT strategy was pending Government approval, and in 2025 it still recommended approving a multi-annual IT programme for customs. No source reports its approval.

The Commission confirms that Moldova signed a cooperation agreement with the European Labour Authority in May 2025. The Government reports that it then began a dialogue with the Authority on priority areas, including EESSI, but this rests on its own account.

The Commission reported in 2025 that efforts to digitalise the public property register were under way and in 2026 that preparations were ongoing, with full operation still pending. The register is not yet digitalised.

The Reform Agenda planned an eHealth strategy and legal framework by 2025, and the Government planned the regulatory framework for electronic health data exchange. Moldova adopted the National Programme for Digitalisation and Innovation in Health 2025-2030, recorded separately, but no source says whether it is this strategy, and no source reports the legal framework adopted.
The Commission reports that the feasibility study on the financial impact of introducing the European Health Insurance Card was finalised in August 2026.

The Commission confirms that Moldova adopted the National Programme for Digitalisation and Innovation in Health 2025-2030, approved by Government Decision No. 556/2025. No source yet reports on its delivery.

The Digital Society Development Programme was planned as one of three programmes under the Digital Transformation Strategy, and an international partner reported in 2024 that the Ministry was developing them. The Government later reports that the three programmes were merged into a single programme, the Implementation Programme 2025-2027, so this programme was not adopted on its own.

The law is in force and is the basis for state information resources and services such as EVOSign. An audit found that the e-Governance Agency had not drafted the methodological frameworks the law requires, so its application is incomplete.

The Government reports that several ministries and the Equality Council are adjusting secondary legislation after Law No. 200/2025, and that the Ministry of Internal Affairs still needs to revise its rules on registering EU citizens. No source reports any of these acts approved.
The law on cybersecurity of 5G networks is planned in the National Accession Programme, with a deadline of December 2027, and no source reports a draft submitted or adopted.
The law on artificial intelligence is planned, with transposition of the EU AI Act foreseen by the end of 2026 or 2027, and no source reports it drafted or adopted.
Interoperability with EU systems managed by eu-LISA is at the stage of a feasibility study and working meetings, and no source reports any national system connected.
The online subsidy application system is planned, with a baseline of 1% for online application modules against a 30% target, and no source reports it launched.
Piloting the generative AI assistant on the EVO portal is planned as a 2026 performance indicator for the e-Governance Agency, with a revised deadline, and no source reports the pilot launched.
The Government reports that the generative AI tool for transposing EU legislation is being piloted and tested, with feedback sent and further testing planned. It is not yet in use.

The e-Governance Agency reports that as National Contact Point for the Digital Europe Programme it supported about 200 institutions and companies and recorded 14 applications to calls in 2025. This rests on its own reporting.

A civil society report states that personal data is protected under a dedicated law and that the National Centre for Personal Data Protection monitors compliance. The source does not give the law's number, so it may refer to Law No. 133/2011, which remains in force until Law No. 195/2024 takes effect.

The strategy ran from 2019 to 2024. The Commission reported in 2021 that the national CERT foreseen by it was still pending, and in 2025 that it had lapsed without addressing new threats, so no source shows its measures carried out.
The Commission reported in 2021 that Moldova benefited from an EU4Digital pilot on mutual recognition of electronic signatures with Ukraine. No later source reports on it.
The Commission reports that the social security agreement with Greece, signed in September 2021, entered into force in January 2023. No source gives data on cases handled under it.
The Commission reported in 2023 that the integrated information system "Migration and asylum" keeps records of migrant workers, which shows it in use. No later source reports on it.
The Commission reported in 2024 that a qualified electronic signature was introduced for company registration and filing with the business register. No source gives data on its use.

The Commission reported in 2024 that online business registration for foreign investors had been introduced, and the Government reports the E-Filing service optimised. No source gives data on its use.
The Commission reports that procurement for the ODA integrated information system was completed in June 2026, so the system is not yet in place.
The Commission reports that the lucrezlegal.md platform for reporting undeclared work was launched in March 2025. No source gives data on reports made through it.
The Commission reports that Moldova has joined and is part of the EU Digital Identity Cooperation Group.

The Reform Agenda sets the target of all declarations submitted to a new e-Integrity system, and in August 2026 the National Integrity Agency put a new concept for the system out to consultation to replace the current one. The new system is not yet in place.

The Commission reports that Government Decision No. 222/2026 was adopted on 1 May 2026 and established the legal framework for the Customs Decisions System, and lists the national system among the customs systems currently operational.

The Government planned in 2024 to create the preconditions for an IGM information system, and the Commission states in 2026 that the Inspectorate's systems still need upgrades for interoperability. No source reports the new system in place.

The Commission reports that in February 2026 Moldova designated the e-Governance Agency as the National Access Point for EESSI, with liaison bodies for social insurance and health insurance. No source reports the access point working, and Moldova is not yet connected to EESSI.

The Commission reports that Moldova has partially aligned its legal framework with the European Maritime Single Window Regulation. Aligning procedures with EMSA's digital systems is still set out by the Government as a priority, and no source reports the systems connected.
The 2023 strategy assigns the shared digital units a role in supporting its implementation, and no source reports how they have carried out that role.

Government Decision No. 822 of 2020 added the regulation on technical administration and maintenance of state information systems to Government Decision No. 414/2018. No source reports how the regulation is applied.

The Government reports that the elections information system has 16 modules, the newest launched in 2025. An audit found its concept had not been updated or aligned with the ICT rules, and no source gives data on its use; the audit item is machine-translated.

The Government lists Law No. 126/2023 on remote identification and interaction among its adopted measures, and an international partner describes the related Contactless Business initiative. No source reports how the law is applied.
The General Inspectorate for Migration reports the draft among the normative drafts it gave opinions on in 2023. No source reports its adoption.
The Ministry of Infrastructure and Regional Development is amending the rules on service housing, and the change appears as a draft Government Decision. No source reports its approval.
The correlation tables with ESCO are planned in the 2025 accession programme. Moldova has designated members of the ESCO Working Group, but no source reports the tables drafted.
The "EU Integration" section on the CNAM website is planned, and no source reports it created.

The Government reports that the EU-Moldova Association Council adopted Decision No. 1/2025 on 4 August 2025, completing the conditions for Roam Like at Home. The Commission confirms that Moldova joined the Roam Like at Home area on 1 January 2026.

The Government reports that Law No. 53/2025 partially transposed Regulation (EU) 2019/1150, and the rules on penalties and enforcement are still missing. The 2025 progress report on the digital strategy gives the number 53/2025 to the geo-blocking law instead, so the law's number should be checked.
The decision on the national cyber incident and crisis response plan appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its approval.

The decision appears as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and the Cyber Security Agency reports that the regulatory framework for state supervision and control in cybersecurity was drafted and approved in 2025. This rests on the Agency's own report, which does not give the decision's number.
The e-Monitoring system is planned, and no source reports it developed or launched.

The National Centre for Personal Data Protection reports that it organised 84 courses and trained over 3,600 people in the reporting period, ahead of the new law taking effect on 23 August 2026. This rests on the Centre's own report.
The programme was approved by Government Decision No. 808 of 23 November 2022 for 2022 to 2025. No source reports on how far its digitalisation priorities were carried out before it ended.
The Centre is set up and working as owner and technical operator of the MTender procurement system, with 424 of 479 posts filled. This rests on government sources.
The single liaison point and cooperation through IMI on posted workers are planned, and no source reports them set up.
Law No. 274/2011 is in force and is described as one of the basic acts governing the employment of foreigners. No source in these items reports how it is applied.

Integrating the Public Services Portal with the EU Single Digital Gateway is planned, and the Government reports only that the public launch of the integrated EVO portal was prepared for January 2026. No source reports the gateway integration.
The amendment to Law No. 234/2021 and the Administrative Code is still listed as a planned action in the 2025 progress report, and no source reports it adopted.
The amendment to Law No. 467/2003 was planned, but the Government reports that the action will be reconsidered depending on changes to the cybersecurity law. No source reports it adopted.

The Government reports that the e-Governance Agency is part of the WE BUILD consortium selected for the second round of large-scale pilots of the European Digital Identity Wallet and is taking part in it. This rests on government sources.

The General Inspectorate for Migration reports that the agreement with France on the International Volunteering in Enterprise Programme was signed on 20 November 2025. No source reports its entry into force or use.
The items mention the National Social Security Information System only in relation to its future interoperability with EESSI and say nothing about the system's own status.

The Government reports that the system's users were extended in 2025 to second-level local authorities and that all 67 central and local authorities submitted their 2025 internal control reports through it. This rests on government reporting.

A 2025 doctoral thesis states that Law No. 180/2008 has been repealed and most of its provisions moved into Law No. 200/2010. The same thesis elsewhere describes it as the main law on the employment procedure, so the source is inconsistent on whether it is still in force.
The only item is a civil society recommendation to increase the number of digital ambassadors, which gives no evidence on the programme's status.

A civil society source reports that the European Commission accepted a proposal to include roaming in the Association Agreement, and the Government reports that Association Council Decision No. 1/2025 amended the relevant annex in August 2025.
A civil society source reports that STISC launched the cyberevent.gov.md platform in June 2024. No source gives data on its use.
A civil society source reports that the law on contracts for the supply of digital content and digital services was adopted in 2024. No source reports how it is applied.
The Commission reported in 2021 that the online tender platform was used for COVID-19 related procurement and that such tenders were monitored. No later source reports on it.

The Commission reported in 2022 that the Government's Action Plan for 2021-2022 contains objectives and actions on digital public services. The plan has expired, and no source reports how far it was carried out.
The Commission reports that Parliament adopted the amendment in first reading in July 2023.

The Government reports that 2023 amendments to Law No. 200/2010 let EU citizens work for 90 days without a residence permit for work, which are recorded as a separate intervention. No source says whether this amendment became that law, so its final status cannot be established.

The Commission reported in 2023 that the social protection information system carries out the registration, granting and payment of social benefits, which shows it in use. No later source reports on it.
The Commission reported in 2023 that Moldova benefited from EU4Digital pilot initiatives including eCustoms. No later source reports on the pilot.
The Commission reports that the business register's paper archive was digitalised between August 2023 and August 2024.
The Commission reported in 2024 that the procedure for obtaining Authorised Economic Operator status was digitalised through an IT solution. No source gives data on its use.
The 2024 Growth Plan Communication proposes expert assistance through the Customs Programme, and no source reports the assistance provided.
The Commission reports that Moldova launched the European Consumer Centre and developed related digital tools. No source reports on its activity.
The Commission reports that the Moldova Instant Payments system was launched and is helping to lower transaction costs. No source gives data on its use.

The Commission refers to the implementation of the Public Services Agency roadmap and asks that it be advanced further to address limited capacity and digitalisation resources. No source describes what has been delivered.
The only item is the Commission's statement that Moldova will have to align with the IT solutions for EMCS and SEED, and no source reports any Moldovan action on SEED.
The Reform Agenda plans a legal framework for digital health services followed by electronic health records, and no item reports the framework approved.
The Commission reports that the World Bank provided a loan for June 2023 to June 2024 to develop the pilot phase of the State Register of Legal Units.
The Commission reports that Moldova adopted Law No. 106 on 11 June 2026, transposing the Gigabit Infrastructure Act. No source yet reports its application.
The Commission reports that further implementing acts on data collection, monitoring and evaluation of EURES activities were adopted in the reporting period.
The Commission reports that the new legal framework reinforced ARCOM's administrative and financial independence. No source reports how it has been applied.
The Commission reports that Moldova adopted the law on the protection of topographies of semiconductor products in April 2026.

The Commission reports that Moldova further advanced its integration into the e-Phyto system in preparation for full TRACES-NT integration, but does not say whether the integration is already working.
The only item is the 2023 strategy's proposal to expand use of the Universal Service and Access Fund, which gives no evidence on the fund's status.
The 2023 strategy plans a National Cyber Security Strategy, and in 2025 the Commission noted that the 2019-2024 strategy had lapsed. No source reports a new strategy adopted.
The 2023 strategy provides for each ministry and central authority to appoint a Digital Transformation Coordinator, and no source reports the appointments.
The only item reports a decision to make SIERUSS interoperable with SIA REA and says nothing about the system's own status. The item is machine-translated, so it is capped at Medium confidence.

According to the e-Governance Agency, the rules in force require authorities to submit their information system concepts to it for coordination, but the problems found arise from deficiencies in applying them. The status rests on one machine-translated audit item, capped at Medium confidence.

An audit reports that the Central Electoral Commission planned and procured the development and piloting of an internet voting system in 2023 and 2024, and no source reports it launched. The status rests on one machine-translated item, capped at Medium confidence.

The Government Activity Plan for 2024 provides for amending the concept and regulation of SIA RFPFP, and no source reports the amendment adopted. The status rests on one machine-translated item, capped at Medium confidence.
The 2024 implementation report plans to develop an indicator passport for the strategy's result indicators, and no source reports it done.
The White Book foresees a later national policy document, action plan and governance framework on data governance and AI, and no source reports them adopted.
The White Book states that the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence was adopted by all 193 member states, including Moldova. No source reports how Moldova applies it.
The General Inspectorate for Migration reports the amendment to Government Decision No. 125/2013 as a draft, and no source reports its approval.

The General Inspectorate for Migration reports that the draft decision listing the states whose citizens may work without a prior right of residence was prepared and sent for promotion. No source reports its approval.
The only item reports a working meeting with the ICT companies' association on improving the rules for foreign IT specialists, and no source reports any change adopted.
The e-Governance Agency lists e-Consulate among its seven new digital platforms. This rests on one government item rated Low confidence, and no source gives data on its use.

The Government reports that the 2023 amendments to Law No. 200/2010 let EU citizens work for 90 days in any 180-day period without a residence permit for work. No source in these items reports how they are applied.
The Government reports that Government Decision No. 617/2024 amended the National Employment Agency's statute, partly aligning it with the EURES Regulation.
The Government reports that Moldova has concluded an agreement on pension rights with Ukraine, based on the territoriality principle. No source gives its date of entry into force or data on its use.

The Government reports that Moldova has concluded an agreement on pension rights with Uzbekistan, based on the territoriality principle. No source gives its date of entry into force or data on its use.
Law No. 198/2020 on voluntary pension funds was adopted, but the Government states that effective implementation of the occupational pension system remains at an early stage.
The law on cross-border medical care appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its adoption.
The amendment to Government Decision No. 230/2020 on CNAS appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its approval.
The amendment to Law No. 198/2020 appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its adoption.
Drafting minimum requirements for processing personal data in EURES data exchange is a planned action, and no source reports them approved.
The Government reports that ANOFM Director Order No. 53 of 28 November 2025 approved the procedure for admission as a EURES member or partner. No source reports any admission under it.
The Government reports that the EU acts on radio spectrum were transposed through amendments to the National Frequency Allocation Table, with the latest update in force from 15 September 2023.
The Government describes interoperability with the European Digital Identity Wallets as a task the e-Governance Agency is carrying out, and no source reports it achieved.
Transposition of the EU Chips Act is planned by the end of 2026, and the Commission reported in 2026 that Moldova had yet to align with it.
The order appears only as a planned act in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its approval.
The amendment to Competition Law No. 183/2012 appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its adoption.
The decision on electronic identification assurance levels appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its approval.
The decision on the national cybersecurity certification system appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its approval.
The law on investments appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its adoption.
Mapping and designating digital platforms active in Moldova is a planned action, and no source reports it carried out.

The only item is a planned action to implement a technical solution for verifying and validating EU-issued signature certificates, which says nothing about the status of Government Decision No. 491/2022 itself.

The Government reports that Law No. 130/2025 amended the Electoral Code, including electronic subscription and voter lists and the use of electronic signatures on them. No source reports how these provisions are applied.
The technical solution for paperless administration is listed as a planned measure, and no source reports it developed.
The Parliament decision approving the cybersecurity policy document is referred to as a draft, and no source reports its adoption.
The Government describes the programme's action plan, including re-engineering of the electronic procurement system. No source reports how far it has been carried out.
The decision on connecting the National Vehicle Register to EUCARIS appears only as a draft in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its approval.
The Government reports that the amendments to Law No. 220/2007, together with the State Register of Legal Units, partially transpose the EU rules on digital tools in company law.
Training of health professionals in e-health is planned for 2027, and no source reports it carried out.
The amendment to Government Decision No. 211/2019 on MConnect appears as a planned act in the 2025 accession programme, and no source reports its approval.
Telemedicine and remote consultation services are a planned action, and no source reports a platform launched.
Digitalising social and employment services is set out as a priority, and no source reports specific measures carried out.
Connection to the CCN Gateway is a planned action with the indicator of an operational connection, and no source reports it achieved.
The network code on cybersecurity of cross-border electricity flows is listed for transposition, and no source reports an ANRE decision adopted.
The Government reports that the national geoportal has been integrated into the INSPIRE Geoportal since 2024. No source gives data on its use.
The only item names the State Register of Legal Acts as a system that the planned e-Monitoring system will connect to and says nothing about its own status.

The Government reports that amendments to Law No. 200/2010 between 2016 and 2024 regulated the admission of EU citizens and simplified residence procedures for foreigners. No source in these items reports how they are applied.
